baseline.note: Studies priced at about $127 intraday; changes are measured from the $125.53 close.

sources: Forensic and investment risk review, 20 November 2026
rule: This file is the original hypothesis. It is never edited. Tracking goes in nvidia-tracker-data.js.

cases.name: Base
cases.condition: Peak, then a gentle step down

steps.question: Does the next quarter clear the air?
steps.context: The full Q3 10-Q is due by 4 December. Then come the SEC inquiry’s scope, the CEO search, and the Q4 report in late February against a $130B guide at a 71 to 72% gross margin.

what_must_happen.strong-bull: The 10-Q adds nothing alarming, the SEC matter stays narrow and a credible permanent CEO is named. Q4 beats $130B at a gross margin of 72% or more, and customers start paying faster.
what_must_happen.bull: Q4 lands at or above $130B with a gross margin of 72% or more. A credible permanent CEO is named and the SEC matter stays narrow. Confidence starts to come back.
what_must_happen.base: Q4 comes in line. The SEC inquiry and the CEO search drag on without escalating, and NVIDIA’s first words on FY29 are cautious. The stock swings between about $100 and $160.
what_must_happen.bear: Q4 is in line, but the gross margin guide slips below 70% and inventory grows faster than revenue for a second quarter. Customers still take more than 65 days to pay.
what_must_happen.severe-bear: The SEC inquiry escalates: a Wells notice or subpoena is disclosed and a restatement becomes possible. Collections slip past 75 days, or a bad-debt charge appears.

early_sign.bull: Q4 gross margin at 72% or more
early_sign.severe-bear: a Wells notice, subpoena or restatement

steps.question: Do the big buyers keep spending in 2027?
steps.context: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle guided $242B to $270B for Q4 2026 and promised significant increases for 2027. They buy 56% of NVIDIA’s data center chips, and several are projected to be cash-negative in 2027.

what_must_happen.strong-bull: The hyperscalers raise their 2027 budgets again and GPU rental prices rise. Demand outruns supply into FY29.
what_must_happen.bull: All five keep the 2027 increases they promised, borrowing where needed, and investors accept the debt.
what_must_happen.base: Budgets still grow, but more slowly, while Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium and Broadcom-built chips keep taking share.
what_must_happen.bear: One hyperscaler, or Oracle, cuts its 2027 budget. One top-five cut matters more than every NVIDIA financing loop combined.
what_must_happen.severe-bear: Two or more of the top five cut. With several already cash-negative, debt markets stop funding the gap.

early_sign.base: custom chips past about 28% of AI servers
early_sign.bear: any top-five buyer flat or down

steps.question: Do the AI labs and neoclouds stay financed?
steps.context: NVIDIA holds $109.7B of stakes, backs $32B of neocloud capacity and guarantees up to $105B of OpenAI’s Ohio leases from FY29. OpenAI expects to burn about $57B in 2027.

what_must_happen.strong-bull: OpenAI and Anthropic beat their revenue plans and neoclouds refinance at tighter spreads. NVIDIA’s stakes gain value and no backstop is used.
what_must_happen.bull: Funding continues on normal terms. The backstops go unused and the Ohio guarantee is never tested.
what_must_happen.base: Money keeps coming, at a higher price. NVIDIA is far more selective with financing deals, as it said on 17 November, and losses stay minor.
what_must_happen.bear: Neocloud refinancing stalls as GPU rental prices fall. Orders slip and backstops come into play: about $25B of losses on commitments.
what_must_happen.severe-bear: OpenAI or a large neocloud misses payments or raises money on distressed terms. Guarantees are called and stakes written down: about $90B of losses, hitting demand, the stake and sentiment at once.

early_sign.severe-bear: a distressed raise or covenant breach

steps.question: What does FY28 deliver?
steps.context: Analysts expect $709B to $726B; management’s outlook is about $740B. $203B of supply purchases fall due in the year, about all its expected cost of goods.

what_must_happen.strong-bull: $780B, up 84% and above management’s outlook, at a 73% gross margin. Every dollar of supply bought for the year is used.
what_must_happen.bull: $740B, management’s ~75% growth, with gross margin back at 72.5% as contracted price rises take effect.
what_must_happen.base: $680B, up 60%: a record year that still misses consensus by about 5%. Gross margin settles at 71%.
what_must_happen.bear: $600B, up 42% but about 15% below consensus, and gross margin falls to 68% as custom chips force price cuts. That is close to the studies’ −30% combination.
what_must_happen.severe-bear: $520B, up 23%, at a 62% gross margin. The $203B of supply due in the year exceeds what sales use, and memory contracts become losses.

steps.question: Is FY28 the peak?
steps.context: Today’s price assumes FY28 is the peak and long-run free cash flow settles near $240B a year. FY29 revenue above about $600B makes today’s price look cheap; below about $420B, expensive.

what_must_happen.strong-bull: No. FY29 grows another 20% to $936B, and free cash flow reaches about $453B, nearly twice what today’s price assumes.
what_must_happen.bull: Only just: FY29 edges up 5% to $777B, with about $367B of free cash flow. The plateau investors fear turns out higher than they priced.
what_must_happen.base: Yes, gently: FY29 falls 10% to $612B and free cash flow to about $279B, close to what today’s price already assumes.
what_must_happen.bear: Yes, sharply: FY29 falls 30% to $420B and free cash flow to about $173B, below the $182B a year at which the studies say the thesis breaks.
what_must_happen.severe-bear: FY29 halves to $260B. Free cash flow of about $84B is below even this year’s level.

early_sign.strong-bull: a first FY29 outlook above FY28
early_sign.base: a modest decline in the FY29 outlook
early_sign.severe-bear: a FY29 outlook down by half

steps.question: What will investors pay?
steps.context: Today the stock trades at about 8 times next year’s expected earnings, against 18 times for the S&P 500. A recovery needs confidence more than earnings.

what_must_happen.strong-bull: 12 times FY29 earnings: about $266, more than double today and above the $239 record. It needs growth beyond FY28 and restored confidence; earnings alone are not enough.
what_must_happen.bull: 10 times: about $180, up 43%. Confidence returns with a permanent CEO and a narrow SEC outcome.
what_must_happen.base: 9 times: about $123, roughly where it is now. Analysts are about right on earnings, but the discount stays.
what_must_happen.bear: 10 times lower earnings: about $84, down a third. Investors look through a weak year, but the earnings have gone.
what_must_happen.severe-bear: 12 times depressed earnings, after about $90B of one-time losses: about $46, down nearly two thirds.
